text: This is Stack Blueprint.
Describe any software idea and it draws the product stack and the exact AI workspace your coding agent needs.
Most agents can name a sensible stack.
For this roommate fridge app, Expo, React Native, and Supabase are reasonable choices.
But picking Expo is not the hard part. Equipping the agent to execute Expo professionally is.
Stack Blueprint uses WebMCP so the browser agent can operate the real planning surface.
I give it the same project description and ask it to build the blueprint.
There is no long questionnaire and no disconnected answer in chat.
The agent calls build_project_blueprint.
The page infers a mobile prototype, consults VibeLeaderboard, and draws the result into shared page state.
The application stack is straightforward. The valuable part is what appears above it.
Expo activates the official Expo MCP and exact project, design, router, animation, and NativeWind skills.
React Doctor, Expo Doctor, and device automation.
Supabase activates its MCP and database guidance. Tools are grouped by role.
Every logo is inspectable, with its role, rationale, and official source.
Production-only services are deliberately deferred when a prototype does not need them.
Vibe Intel is not a random article feed.
Stack Blueprint converts relevant evidence into instructions the agent can execute.
Define acceptance criteria. Use a fresh evaluator. Keep repository context explicit.
Require user-visible verification.
Because this is WebMCP, the person and agent work on the same object.
The person can explore the drawing while the agent can inspect, refine, and render the plan.
The final brief carries the stack, workspace, evidence, and build order into implementation.
Stack Blueprint equips the agent to build better.
